correctness.summary: For connected bipartite graphs, diss<=n-1 and alpha>=ceil(n/2). Equality in the resulting gap bound forces diss=n-1 and alpha=ceil(n/2); deleting the unique vertex outside a maximum dissociation set leaves only K1/K2 components, and bipartiteness forces exactly one center edge into each component, yielding a subdivided star. Solving its independence formula gives the complete parity-sensitive classification. Finite verification agrees.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The accessible full text of the most directly relevant 2023 dissociation-vs-independence paper was checked, together with dissociation/3-path-cover literature and synonymous searches. No fixed-order gap theorem or equivalent complete equality classification was found in the checked sources or current SCOPE records.

value.summary: The result gives an exact fixed-order extremum over all connected bipartite graphs, proves that every extremal is necessarily a tree, classifies all extremal isomorphism classes for every order, and equivalently determines the largest possible difference between ordinary and 3-path vertex-cover numbers.

limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge; unindexed or differently phrased equivalent results may exist.
The dual 3-path vertex-cover terminology is the main residual source of possible prior coverage.
The theorem is stated for finite simple connected bipartite graphs.
